Consider $△PQR$ shown above. The line segment $\overset{―}{RH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overset{―}{PQ}.$ If $m∠PQR={105}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠QRH.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HQR+m∠PQR & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HQR+{105}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HQR & ={75}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $△QHR$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠QRH+m∠HQR+m∠RHQ & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH+{75}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH+{165}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH & ={15}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
